summary: Tested new Staff Attendance + Payroll feature (backend + frontend). All 9 pytest cases passed (1 skipped then re-run once staff user was created — also passed). Frontend Attendance page loads for super_admin under 'Office' collapsible group, all 4 tabs (Who's in / Regularize / Leave / Payroll) render without console errors, payroll table renders staff rows.
critical_code_review_comments: Attendance.jsx (642 lines) exceeds the 700-line soft limit only marginally, but CheckInCard + PayrollSection + SalaryEditor could each be extracted into their own files under components/attendance/ for maintainability.

routers/attendance.py contains dead code: sweep_late_checkins() is defined but intentionally not wired (per problem statement) — consider guarding behind a feature flag or removing until enabled to avoid confusion.

Backend check-in endpoint doesn't validate that user has role in ('staff','office_admin','super_admin') — a role='user' account with attendance='edit' (impossible via defaults but possible via permission override) could check in. Low risk given USER_DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS.attendance='none'.

The /api/attendance/board endpoint does NOT include role=super_admin users in the roster (only staff/office_admin). This is intentional but should be documented for admins who wonder why they don't appear on the 'Who's in' board.
STAFF_DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS gives 'attendance'='edit' correctly; PERMISSION_PAGES includes 'attendance'; USER_DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS.attendance='none' — all consistent.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Attendance feature is stable. Backend tests live in /app/backend/tests/test_attendance.py. Run with `pytest backend/tests/test_attendance.py -o addopts=`. Note pytest.ini uses xdist by default — must override addopts. Payroll test depends on at least one staff/office_admin user existing in the tenant; test creates one if missing.
